extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners; patent practitioners and applicants
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and quality/formatting standards from the MPEP for preparing and examining patent specifications, substitute specifications, marks/trade names, copyright/mask work notices, and drawings (including when drawings are required and their technical requirements).

rubrics_metrics.name: Substitute specification entry under 37 CFR 1.125
rubrics_metrics.description: A substitute specification which complies with 37 CFR 1.125 should normally be entered; a substitute specification is not permitted in a reissue application or in a reexamination proceeding (37 CFR 1.125(d)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a substitute specification filed under 37 CFR 1.125(b) and (c) is denied entry, it should be so marked and applicant notified (use form paragraph 6.28.02). Typical examiner reasons to insert: missing statement as to lack of new matter under 37 CFR 1.125(b); missing marked-up copy in addition to clean copy; missing clean copy in addition to marked-up copy; filed in a reissue or reexamination proceeding; filed after payment of the issue fee; or contains claims. Substitute specifications filed after final action or appeal are governed by 37 CFR 1.116; those filed after mailing of a notice of allowance are governed by 37 CFR 1.312. See MPEP § 714.20 for entry of amendments which substitute specification and MPEP § 608.04 for new matter in amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on derogatory remarks about others' prior art
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant may refer to the general state of the art and the advance made by the invention, but is not permitted to make derogatory or disparaging remarks concerning the inventions, products, or processes of any particular person other than the applicant, or statements as to the merits or validity of applications or patents of another person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mere comparisons with the prior art are not considered disparaging per se. Examiners should ensure specification language avoids disparaging statements; treat permissible statements as comparisons describing advance over prior art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restoration of canceled matter (37 CFR 1.121)
rubrics_metrics.description: Canceled text in the specification can be reinstated only by a subsequent amendment presenting the previously canceled matter as a new insertion (37 CFR 1.121(b)(4)). A claim canceled by amendment (deleted in its entirety) may be reinstated only by a subsequent amendment presenting the claim as a new claim with a new claim number (37 CFR 1.121(c)(5)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reinstatement is not by simple reactivation of prior-canceled material; it must be introduced as new matter in a later amendment (subject to new-matter rules). See MPEP § 714 for handling canceled matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transfer/use of specification or drawings in subsequent applications
rubrics_metrics.description: No part of a specification or drawings can normally be transferred to another application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Generally, specification and drawings are not transferable between applications (see MPEP § 608.02(i)). Examiners should treat attempted transferals cautiously and follow MPEP guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of marks/trade names in specification — identification requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A mark or trade name may be used in a patent application to identify an article, product, service, or organization only if (A) its meaning is established by an accompanying definition in the specification which is sufficiently descriptive, enabling, precise and definite such that a claim including the mark or trade name complies with 35 U.S.C. 112, or (B) its meaning is well‑known to one skilled in the relevant art and is satisfactorily defined in the literature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Condition (A) or (B) must be met at the time of filing of the complete application (see examples such as United States Gypsum Co. v. National Gypsum Co.). If the identification is omitted and deemed necessary, the examiner should hold the disclosure insufficient and reject claims based solely on the mark/trade name. If the product/service identity requires further description (e.g., process of manufacture), such an amendment may be permitted only if it does not introduce new matter and is supported by satisfactory showings that the characteristic was known at filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification introduced by amendment must be limited to known characteristics
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the identification of a mark or trade name is introduced by amendment, it must be restricted to the characteristics of the product, service, or organization known at the time the application was filed to avoid any question of new matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments adding identification cannot introduce new matter beyond what was known at filing. Examiners should verify that added identification does not raise new-matter issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proprietary nature of marks — capitalization and prevention of misuse
rubrics_metrics.description: The proprietary nature of marks should be respected; marks should be identified by capitalizing each letter (for word/letter marks) or otherwise indicating the mark (for symbols or devices).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Every effort should be made to prevent use in any manner which might adversely affect the mark's validity as a trademark or service mark. Examiners may conduct a Trademark Search on the USPTO website to determine whether an apparent mark is registered and to which goods it applies. Form paragraph 6.20 may be used to inform applicant of the proprietary nature of marks used in commerce. The examiner should replace marks with appropriate generic terminology where misuse is demonstrated and the application is still pending.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preferred and prohibited phrasing when referencing marks/trade names
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner should not permit language such as 'the product X (a descriptive name) commonly known as Y (trade name or mark)'; language such as 'the product X (a descriptive name) sold under the trademark Y' is permissible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid wording that fails to make clear that a term is a trade name or mark; require capitalization or proper trademark symbol where appropriate. Use form paragraph 6.20 to communicate required changes to applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyright and mask work notices — authorization and placement
rubrics_metrics.description: A copyright or mask work notice may be placed in a design or utility patent application adjacent to the copyright or mask work material, but inclusion is permitted only if the authorization language set forth in 37 CFR 1.71(e) is included at the beginning (preferably as the first paragraph) of the specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The content of the notice must be limited to only those elements provided for by law (examples: '©1983 John Doe' and '*M* John Doe'). For notices in drawings see § 1.84(s). If the required authorization language is not included, the notice will be objected to as improper; if the examiner maintains the objection, a petition under 37 CFR 1.181 may be filed. Inclusion after a Notice of Allowance is permitted only if criteria of 37 CFR 1.312 are satisfied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyright/mask work notice formatting in drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: A copyright or mask work notice may appear in a drawing but must be placed within the sight of the drawing immediately below the figure representing the copyright or mask work material and be limited to letters having a print size of .32 cm to .64 cm (1/8 to 1/4 inches) high.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If placed on a drawing in conformance with these provisions, the notice will not be objected to as extraneous matter under 37 CFR 1.84. Inclusion is subject to the authorization language requirement in 37 CFR 1.71(e) (preferably as the first paragraph of the specification).

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawing requirement where necessary for understanding (35 U.S.C. 113 & 37 CFR 1.81)
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant shall furnish a drawing of the invention where necessary for the understanding of the subject matter to be patented (35 U.S.C. 113). For design applications, a drawing is required to be entitled to a filing date (35 U.S.C. 171). For applications filed on or after December 18, 2013 (except design), 35 U.S.C. 111 no longer requires a drawing for a filing date, but 35 U.S.C. 113 still requires a drawing where necessary for understanding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Absence of a drawing where necessary may prevent obtaining a patent for claimed invention if drawings later cannot cure insufficiency. Applicants should be prudent and include drawings where necessary. Examiners should require drawings where needed under 37 CFR 1.81 and follow OPAP determinations regarding whether drawings are 'necessary' for filing-date purposes for applications filed before Dec 18, 2013.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of drawings submitted after filing date
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawings submitted after the filing date may not be used (i) to overcome any insufficiency of the specification due to lack of an enabling disclosure or otherwise inadequate disclosure therein, or (ii) to supplement the original disclosure for the purpose of interpretation of the scope of any claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Drawings submitted post-filing that introduce new matter should not be entered; if entered, they cannot be used to expand or supply missing enabling disclosure. Examiners must describe new matter found in substitute or additional drawings in the next Office action and may refuse entry.

rubrics_metrics.name: OPAP and process for determining whether drawings are 'necessary' (pre-PLT filing-date rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: For applications filed under 35 U.S.C. 111 before December 18, 2013, a drawing (where necessary for understanding) or a high quality copy thereof must be filed with the application to be entitled to a filing date. OPAP will make the initial decision whether a drawing is 'necessary' under the first sentence of 35 U.S.C. 113.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If OPAP determines drawings required and none were filed, applicant will be notified and a filing date will not be granted until drawing is received (37 CFR 1.53(e)). If an examiner believes a filing date should not have been granted because drawings were required, the SPE should review and may request cancellation of the filing date with a memorandum identifying the subject matter requiring illustration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim types where drawings are not required for filing date (pre-PLT exceptions)
rubrics_metrics.description: For applications filed before December 18, 2013, a drawing is not required for a filing date under pre-PLT 35 U.S.C. 111 if the application contains: (A) at least one process claim including the term 'process' or 'method' in its introductory phrase; (B) at least one composition claim including 'composition,' 'compound,' 'mixture' or 'pharmaceutical' in its introductory phrase; (C) at least one claim directed to a coated article or product or an article made from a particular material; (D) at least one claim directed to a laminated article or product; or (E) at least one claim where the sole distinguishing feature is the presence of a particular material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 601.01(f) for more complete explanation. These exceptions affect whether OPAP treats an application without drawings as incomplete for filing-date purposes under pre-PLT rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement procedure when subject matter admits of illustration by a drawing (form paragraphs 6.23 / 6.23.01)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the subject matter admits of illustration by a drawing and none was furnished, the examiner should require submission of a drawing under 37 CFR 1.81(c). Use form paragraph 6.23 (or 6.23.01 when no examination of claims yet) to require a drawing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When requiring drawings before examination use form paragraph 6.23.01 with a PTOL-90 or PTO-90C cover sheet. No new matter may be introduced in the required drawing. Applicant is given a shortened statutory period of TWO (2) MONTHS to submit a drawing in compliance with 37 CFR 1.81; extensions under 37 CFR 1.136(a) are possible but cannot extend reply beyond SIX MONTHS statutory maximum (35 U.S.C. 133). Failure to timely submit results in ABANDONMENT of the application. Examiners should specifically request at least an ink sketch or permanent print as part of the reply to facilitate early sufficiency determination and absence of new matter (see 37 CFR 1.121 and 1.81(d)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Black-and-white drawing standards (ink requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Black and white drawings are normally required; India ink, or its equivalent that secures solid black lines, must be used for drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Drawings should use solid black lines to ensure reproducibility. Color is only permitted under limited circumstances (see separate criteria). Examiners may require drawings in lieu of photographs if subject admits of illustration by drawing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Color drawings — restricted acceptance and petition requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Color drawings are permitted in design applications; on rare occasions they may be necessary as the only practical medium in a utility patent application. Color drawings will be accepted in utility applications only after granting a petition explaining why color drawings are necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any petition for color drawings must include: (i) the fee set forth in § 1.17(h); (ii) one set of color drawings if submitted via USPTO electronic filing system, or three sets if not; and (iii) an amendment to the specification inserting specified language as the first paragraph of the brief description of the drawings indicating the file contains at least one color drawing and that copies with color drawing(s) will be provided upon request and payment of fee. International (PCT) applications generally do not permit color drawings (PCT Rule 11.13).

rubrics_metrics.name: Photographs — limited acceptance and quality requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Photographs, including photocopies of photographs, are not ordinarily permitted in utility and design patent applications but will be accepted if photographs are the only practicable medium for illustrating the claimed invention (examples: electrophoresis gels, immunological blots, photomicrographs, animals, plants, in vivo imaging, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the subject admits of illustration by a drawing, the examiner may require a drawing instead of a photograph. Photographs must be of sufficient quality such that all details are reproducible in the printed patent. Color photographs are accepted only if conditions for color drawings and black and white photographs are satisfied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of drawings (top-margin information and labeling)
rubrics_metrics.description: Identifying indicia should be provided and, if provided, should include the title of the invention, inventor's name, and application number or docket number (if no application number yet). If provided, this information must be placed on the front of each sheet within the top margin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each drawing sheet submitted after the filing date must be labeled in the top margin as either 'Replacement Sheet' or 'New Sheet' pursuant to 37 CFR 1.121(d). If a marked-up copy of any amended drawing figure including annotations is filed, such marked-up copy must be clearly labeled as 'Annotated Sheet' pursuant to 37 CFR 1.121(d)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Graphic forms in drawings (formulae, tables, waveforms)
rubrics_metrics.description: Chemical or mathematical formulae, tables, and waveforms may be submitted as drawings and are subject to the same requirements as drawings. Each chemical or mathematical formula must be labeled as a separate figure, and each group of waveforms must be presented as a single figure using a common vertical axis with time on the horizontal axis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each individual waveform discussed in the specification must be identified with a separate letter designation adjacent to the vertical axis. Use brackets when necessary to show integration of information and ensure proper labeling of separate figures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paper quality and one-sidedness for drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawings must be made on paper which is flexible, strong, white, smooth, non-shiny, and durable; sheets must be reasonably free from cracks, creases, and folds, and only one side of the sheet may be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each sheet must be reasonably free from erasures, alterations, overwritings, and interlineations. Photographs must be developed on paper meeting sheet-size and margin requirements. Examiners should reject or object to drawings not meeting these physical standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawing sheet size requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: All drawing sheets in an application must be the same size. Acceptable sizes: (1) 21.0 cm by 29.7 cm (DIN A4), or (2) 21.6 cm by 27.9 cm (8 1/2 by 11 inches).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One of the shorter sides is regarded as the top. Maintain consistency across all sheets in the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawing margin requirements and sight dimensions
rubrics_metrics.description: Sheets must not contain frames around the sight but should have scan target points printed on two cater-corner margin corners. Margins: top at least 2.5 cm (1 inch); left at least 2.5 cm (1 inch); right at least 1.5 cm (5/8 inch); bottom at least 1.0 cm (3/8 inch).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These margins leave a maximum sight no greater than 17.0 cm by 26.2 cm on A4 or 17.6 cm by 24.4 cm on 8 1/2 by 11 inch sheets. Do not include frames around the sight; adhere to scan target point guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Views — include as many views as necessary
rubrics_metrics.description: The drawing must contain as many views as [necessary to] ... (i.e., include as many views as are necessary to show the invention).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the drawings present sufficient views to understand the claimed subject matter and to avoid ambiguity or insufficiency. (Text truncated in source, but principle is to include all necessary views.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling substitute or additional drawings that introduce new matter
rubrics_metrics.description: If the examiner discovers new matter in a substitute or additional drawing, the drawing should not be entered and the examiner should describe the new matter that resulted in non-entry in the next Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 6.37 (MPEP § 608.02(h)) where appropriate. The examiner's decision not to enter a drawing for new matter is reviewable by petition under 37 CFR 1.181; the TC Director decides such a petition. If a new drawing without new matter is needed, the examiner may require it under 37 CFR 1.81 or 1.83.
